cf.title: pg_rewind does not rewind diverging timelines

input.subject: pg_rewind does not rewind diverging timelines

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated and several independent people confirm it, so levels 1a and 1b pass. The design is still open at level 2. The UUID is only in the history file, so pg_rewind's own archive reads can still pick the other branch's segment (replication-ondisk-1), and the proposal does not say which timeline comparisons must use the UUID (maintenance-fit-1). The back-branch intent conflicts with the format and API change (standards-compat-1).

brief.title: pg_rewind: detect independent same-TLI promotions with UUIDs in history files
brief.problem: Two servers can promote on their own to the same timeline ID, with identical history entries (same TLI, same switchpoint LSN). pg_rewind then treats them as one timeline, so it skips the rewind or picks a too-late common ancestor and leaves diverged data on the target. This affects HA setups with repeated crashes during failover, with or without a shared archive.
brief.proposed_design: Each promotion generates a UUIDv7 and writes it as an optional fourth field in each timeline history file entry. pg_rewind compares TLI and UUID both in the common ancestor search and in the same-TLI shortcut, and walks back on a mismatch. A zero UUID (old history file) counts as different from a non-zero UUID; the WAL and the end-of-recovery record are unchanged.
user_visible_surface: Timeline history file format: optional UUID field per entry.
pg_rewind behaviour: same-TLI shortcut and ancestor search now also compare UUIDs.
C API: writeTimeLineHistory() gains a UUID argument.
C API: generate_uuidv7_r() and generate_uuidv7() exported in utils/uuid.h.
Backend: malformed UUID in a history file causes FATAL at startup, while pg_rewind treats it as unknown.
author_claims: The scenario is real, was found by a TLA+ model, and can cause silent divergence between servers.
The fix is small and touches few places, so the risk is low.
Even a shared archive cannot guarantee unique TLI assignment, because it is a consensus problem.
The UUID is an extra check, comparable to page checksums, and does not replace the TLI.
Clusters with old history files and a missing target history file keep working.
brief.thread_state: Japin Li and Surya Poondla approved earlier versions, and Andreas Karlsson and Ants Aasma confirm the problem in practice. Michael Paquier opposes a second timeline identifier as unneeded; Ants Aasma says it does not go far enough without the UUID in WAL page headers, and the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: The CF entry targets version 18 and is tagged Bugfix, but the patch changes the history file format and a C function signature, and the thread does not settle back-branch handling.
The patch does not say how old releases or external tools that parse history files react to the fourth field.
The patch does not say whether recovery or restore_command use the UUID, or only pg_rewind.
The thread does not say whether a zero UUID against a non-zero UUID can force needless rewinds after a minor-version upgrade.
No documentation hunks are shown for the history file format or pg_rewind.

prior_attempts.title: Add timeline to partial WAL segments
prior_attempts.quote: As nothing has happened here, I have marked the patch as RwF.
prior_attempts.reason: The author stopped working on it. After discussion, Michael Paquier agreed with a revised scheme in which pg_receivewal would also use the timeline-suffixed name. The author then marked the patch Waiting on Author because it needed more work, and no new version followed for about 20 months. Robert Haas and Michael Paquier also objected to back-patching the naming change into minor releases, but that did not decide the entry.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 renamed archived .partial segments to avoid archive conflicts after several promotions. This proposal adds a per-promotion UUID to history file entries and changes only pg_rewind matching, not WAL file names.

objections.title: Archived WAL segments with the same TLI stay ambiguous to pg_rewind
objections.failure_scenario: S1 and S2 both promote to TLI 2 and share an archive, which then holds 000000020000000000000004 from S2. pg_rewind --restore-target-wal on S1 correctly backs up to TLI 1, then restores that segment as S1's own TLI 2 WAL. It misses S1's changed blocks, and S1 keeps diverged pages with no error.
objections.argument: The UUID lives only in the history file, so nothing ties a WAL segment to the promotion that wrote it. Message #23 raises this and proposes the UUID in XLogLongPageHeaderData. Message #27 calls WAL format changes too intrusive but does not show that pg_rewind's own archive reads are safe. The fix covers ancestor selection and leaves block collection in the same collision.
objections.author_must_show: When pg_rewind restores target WAL from a shared archive after two same-TLI promotions, what stops it from reading the other branch's segment of the same name?

critic.reasoning: Message #23 raises same-TLI segments in a shared archive, and message #27 answers for recovery but not for pg_rewind's own archive reads. The case needs a missing local segment, so it is narrow, but the thread does not rule it out.

objections.title: Second timeline identity checked only by pg_rewind
objections.failure_scenario: Two nodes promote to TLI 2 and both archive WAL. Recovery or restore_command later replays the wrong node's TLI 2 segments, because only pg_rewind compares the UUID. Operators find out after the restore, when the data has diverged.
objections.argument: The patch makes the UUID part of timeline identity but checks it in one frontend tool. Recovery, the archiver and WAL page headers ignore it. Ants Aasma (message #23) gives the archive case, and the author's reply in message #27 does not close it. Any future code that compares timelines would also need to check the UUID, and nothing fails if it does not.
objections.author_must_show: Which other code paths that compare timelines must honour the UUID, and how would a future change that misses one be caught?

critic.reasoning: The recovery scenario exists today and the patch does not make it worse, so fatal is too strong. The proposal still does not say which timeline comparisons use the UUID and which do not, as message #23 asks.

objections.title: Bugfix tag and back-branch intent conflict with format and API changes
objections.failure_scenario: A packager ships a minor release with this fix. An HA tool or extension built against the old writeTimeLineHistory() signature breaks on the minor update. In a rolling minor upgrade, patched and unpatched nodes then write history files in two formats in the same cluster and archive.
objections.argument: The CF entry is tagged Bugfix and targets version 18. The patch changes the timeline history file format and the signature of an exported backend function. Message #17 asked whether the signature change is an ABI break if the fix is back-patched, and no later message answers it. A committer would likely ask for a master-only design, or a separate back-branch variant that keeps the old signature and file format.
objections.author_must_show: Is this meant for master only, and if not, how does a back-branch version keep the writeTimeLineHistory() ABI and the history file format stable within a major release?

critic.reasoning: The CF entry says Bugfix with target 18, and message #17's ABI question on writeTimeLineHistory() has no answer in the thread. The patch prose has no back-branch plan, so the question stands.

objections.title: History file format change has no stated contract for external parsers
objections.failure_scenario: A backup or HA tool reads a new history file, from the archive or through the TIMELINE_HISTORY replication command, and splits each line on tabs. It shows the UUID as the switch reason, or rejects a line with an unexpected field count. The operator finds out during a failover or a restore.
objections.argument: History files are read by more than the server and pg_rewind: they travel through archives and replication to tools the project does not control. The proposal adds an optional fourth field, but the patch contains no documentation hunk. It does not say where the field sits relative to the free-text reason, or how an older server or older tool should treat it. [P22] shows that a change in field count broke replication utilities across versions, and that commit was reverted.
objections.author_must_show: What is the exact new line layout, where is it documented, and how do older servers and existing tools that parse history files read a line with the UUID field?

precedents.title: Revert "Fix bug in checking of IDENTIFY_SYSTEM result."

critic.reasoning: The patch prose shows no documentation of the new line layout and no statement on older readers. P22 concerns the IDENTIFY_SYSTEM result, not history files, so it should not be used as support.

refuted.title: Startup FATAL on a history file field that recovery never uses
refuted.failure_scenario: A standby restores a history file whose fourth field is damaged or was written by an external tool. With the patch, the standby stops with FATAL at startup and will not replay WAL. Today the same file is accepted, and pg_rewind treats the field as unknown.
refuted.argument: The brief and message #21 show that the backend FATALs on a malformed UUID while pg_rewind ignores it. The backend does not use the UUID for recovery or timeline choice. So the patch adds a new way for a standby to fail to start, on data that has no effect on the server. Message #29 says this split is intended but gives no reason why the backend must be strict.
refuted.author_must_show: Since recovery does not use the UUID, why should a malformed UUID stop the server from starting instead of being treated as unknown, as pg_rewind does?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 notes that the existing syntax-error paths in readTimeLineHistory() use FATAL on purpose, and the author matched them in message #4. The patch follows existing practice for a malformed history file.

refuted.title: Bugfix entry changes the history file format and an exported function
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer back-patches this as a bug fix. An extension built against the older minor release calls writeTimeLineHistory() with the old argument list and breaks after the minor update. Tools that read history files start to see a fourth field in a minor release.
refuted.argument: The CF entry is tagged Bugfix and targets 18, but the patch adds a UUID argument to writeTimeLineHistory() and a new field to an on-disk file. Message #17 flags the ABI break, and the thread does not answer it. The material has no plan for back branches, and no statement on how external readers of history files react to the new field.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this meant for master only, and if not, how do back branches get the fix without changing writeTimeLineHistory() or the history file format?

precedents.title: Add timeline to partial WAL segments

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. P5 was returned because the author stopped working on it, so it adds no support.

refuted.title: Committer in the area opposes the mechanism
refuted.failure_scenario: The patch is committed over the objection of the committer who usually owns this code. A later bug report about UUID mismatches or extra rewinds then has no owner who supports the design. The fix waits for someone willing to defend it.
refuted.argument: Michael Paquier (message #22) calls a second timeline identifier unneeded and says the archive design must guarantee unique TLIs. The supporters in messages #5, #13 and #24 are not committers. In message #32 the author agrees that a DCS-supplied TLI would help and keeps the UUID as a last-resort check. So the project could end up maintaining two mechanisms for one problem.
refuted.author_must_show: Which committer familiar with timelines and pg_rewind will own this, and why is the UUID still needed if the TLI can be coordinated as message #31 proposes?

critic.reasoning: Messages #23, #24 and #26 answer the premise that an archive can guarantee unique TLIs, and message #31 keeps the UUID as a last-resort check beside a coordinated TLI. Ownership belongs in the committability field, which the rubric keeps apart from the verdict.

refuted.title: Format and API change filed as a back-patchable bugfix
refuted.failure_scenario: A minor release starts writing a fourth field in history files. A backup or HA tool that parses those files breaks after the minor upgrade. An extension that calls writeTimeLineHistory() also stops building or linking.
refuted.argument: The CF entry targets 18 and is tagged Bugfix. The patch changes the history file format and the signature of writeTimeLineHistory(). Zsolt Parragi raised the ABI break in message #17, and the thread has no answer to it. The proposal also does not say how older releases or external tools read the new field, and the history file format would stay fixed from then on.
refuted.author_must_show: Is this intended for master only, and how do older releases and tools that parse history files handle the new field?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1 for the back-patch and ABI part, and of standards-compat-2 for external parsers.

questions: When pg_rewind restores target WAL from a shared archive after two same-TLI promotions, what stops it from reading the other branch's segment of the same name?
Which code paths that compare timelines must use the UUID, which may ignore it, and how would a future change that misses one be caught?

committability.owner_note: Michael Paquier takes part in the thread but opposes a second timeline identifier (message #22). The owner must know timeline history handling, promotion in StartupXLOG() and pg_rewind.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the history file format for all later releases, for pg_rewind correctness in mixed old and new clusters, and for any back-branch variant.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted nine versions up to message #33 and answered review comments. The CF entry needs a rebase since 2026-10-22.

priority.reason: HA users who run pg_rewind after failover are affected, and messages #19, #23 and #24 report the problem in practice. The patch is about 44 KiB across xlog.c, timeline.c and pg_rewind, and the thread has not agreed on whether a UUID in the history file alone is the right scope.

provisional_note: Only 3 of 36 messages and no code were read. How the patch parses the fourth field next to the free-text reason, and how pg_rewind picks WAL segments after the ancestor search, could not be checked.

precedents_retrieved.title: Archive current timeline history file on archiver startup if needed
precedents_retrieved.summary: When a primary on a timeline above 1 has WAL archiving enabled after its last timeline switch, the history file for its current timeline is never archived. This breaks cascading standbys and explicit-timeline PITR built from `-X none` base backups. The patch proposed archiving that history file if it is not yet archived, first at archiver startup and later at the end of StartupXLOG, with an alternative patch letting recovery proceed when the initial timeline's history file cannot be fetched.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Kyotaro Horiguchi objected to archiving the same file repeatedly. Robert Haas rejected the alternative of fetching the history file and ignoring errors, and asked whether the two patches were alternatives. After Robert Haas's review the author did not reply, the entry was set to Waiting on Author, and it was later returned with feedback because the feedback had not been addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems to me that trying to fetch a timeline history file and then
ignoring any error has got to be wrong.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical Decoding with timelines
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes logical decoding in the walsender follow timeline changes, as physical replication does, so that logical replication can cascade from a standby. It moved the walsender's send-pointer and timeline logic into shared functions used by both physical and logical sending.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs, the author, withdrew it as Returned with Feedback and said he had a new approach for the next release. Andres Freund noted that it covers only the walsender, while logical decoding also runs through SQL functions. He also said it does not let decoding start on a standby, which also needs forced hot_standby_feedback and slot cleanup in dbase_redo. Michael Paquier reported that the patch no longer applied, the earlier review comments were unaddressed, and no tests were shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Afaics the patch as is won't allow to start logical decoding on a standby.

precedents_retrieved.title: get current and recovery timeline
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set out to let tools read the current timeline of a standby from shared memory, first by allowing pg_walfile_name() on a standby and later through new functions that return the LSN and timeline together. The last version changed pg_stat_get_wal_receiver() to return the last known values when no WAL receiver runs, and added applied_lsn and applied_tli columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected to the last version because pg_stat_wal_receiver maps one to one to the shared memory state of a running WAL receiver, and applied WAL belongs to the startup process. He also did not want to change the check that returns NULL when no WAL receiver is ready, on security grounds. He suggested a separate view over XLogCtl, such as pg_stat_recovery, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
pg_stat_wal_receiver is just a one-one mapping with the shared memory
state of the WAL receiver itself and show data *if and only if* a WAL
receiver is running and iff it is ready to display any data, so I'd
rather not change its nature and it has nothing to do with the state
of WAL being applied by the startup process.  So this gets a -1 from
me.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add timeline to partial WAL segments
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the timeline that a promoted server switches to into the name of the .partial WAL segment it archives, for example 000000010000000100000001.00000002.partial. This prevents archive conflicts when several promotions in HA setups produce the same .partial file; prioritizing .history files in the archiver was proposed alongside it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped working on it. After discussion, Michael Paquier agreed with a revised scheme in which pg_receivewal would also use the timeline-suffixed name. The author then marked the patch Waiting on Author because it needed more work, and no new version followed for about 20 months. Robert Haas and Michael Paquier also objected to back-patching the naming change into minor releases, but that did not decide the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As nothing has happened here, I have marked the patch as RwF.

precedents_retrieved.title: [BUG] Panic due to incorrect missingContrecPtr after promotion
precedents_retrieved.summary: After a standby skipped a missing continuation record, missingContrecPtr stayed set, so on promotion the server wrote an overwrite_contrecord at a past LSN and later hit a WAL flush PANIC. The patch writes the overwrite_contrecord only when missingContrecPtr is ahead of the last WAL record, and adds a TAP test.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was not committed because a separate commit, 6672d79, fixed the same issue. Robert Haas pointed to that commit, and the author confirmed it fixes the PANIC. Before that, Kyotaro Horiguchi's debugging of the author's logs suggested the inconsistent WAL came from the primary.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: For the benefit of anyone who may be looking at this thread in the archive later, I believe this commit will have fixed this issue:

precedents_retrieved.summary: Logical decoding timeline following take II

precedents_retrieved.title: Restrict pg_rewind to specified/needed directories
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, David Steele, Stephen Frost
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_rewind synchronize only a fixed list of directories (base, global, pg_wal, pg_xact and other WAL-related directories), so it no longer copies logs, replication slots or configuration files from the source. The list of files is fetched with one query per listed directory.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers objected to an include list: a directory missing from it, such as one added by a new feature or an extension, can make a rewind silently corrupt. They asked pg_rewind to reuse the exclude list that base backups already use, by moving it to common code, and to add an option for more exclusions. The patch stayed in Waiting on Author, and Michael Paquier returned it with feedback and said he would work on the exclude-list approach himself.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Forgetting something in the
exclusion list just makes the process less efficient while forgetting
something in the inclusion list may mean breakage.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid Copying WAL Segments Before Divergence to Speed Up pg_rewind
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_rewind skip copying WAL segments that come before the segment holding the last common checkpoint, since source and target share them. The author reported that WAL files are over 95% of the data pg_rewind copies in their setups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not answer Michael Paquier's review of 2022-10-06, so the entry was marked returned with feedback. That review asked for tests that use command_checks_all() instead of reading log files, and an assertion that the WAL segment exists on both sides. It also asked about segments with older timelines and for WAL segments to be tracked in file_entry_t. Alexander Korotkov saw no design objections in the thread.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This review has been done a few weeks ago, and there has been no
update since, so I am marking this entry as returned with feedback in
the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow PostgreSQL to perform promote/pause/shutdown operations at end-of-the-wal when the recovery does not reach the recovery target
precedents_retrieved.summary: The proposal stops recovery from promoting at the end of available WAL when the recovery target was not reached, with a new setting (recovery_target_incomplete) to promote, pause or shut down instead. It later split into a second patch that refuses to start WAL replay when the recovery target lies before the restored backup's position, checked against pg_control.
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Steele found the start-point check incorrect: it uses the checkpoint in pg_control, but backup recovery starts from the backup_label checkpoint, and PITR can only start at backup end. The check would accept invalid targets in long backups and reject valid ones, and the last completed xid says little about commit order. He also noted that no consensus existed for the behaviour change, and returned the patch at the end of the CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My point is that the
information you are working from (whatever checkpoint happens to be in
pg_control when recovery starts) is not sufficient for the task.  This
method is inaccurate and would disallow valid recovery scenarios.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent was rejected or reverted for a reason that applies to this proposal. P5 died because work stopped, and its back-patching concern appears only in an AI summary. In message #22, Michael Paquier cites the project's position that unique TLI assignment depends on the archive, and message #31 links a built-in consensus thread, but neither reports an earlier rejection of this idea.
The material contains no new SQL syntax, GUC, psql change or pg_dump object, so these points need no objection.
Objections were found from this angle.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. The UUID is written only into timeline history files that the server or pg_rewind creates, and only the server and pg_rewind read it. No SQL function, role, view or GUC is added, and the history file stays as readable as it is today. A malformed UUID causes FATAL at startup, which matches the existing FATAL paths for malformed history files, and the archive is already trusted input. The use-after-free in the error path (messages #17, #21) was a code defect and was fixed in the thread.
Hot-path cost is not a concern here. The UUID is written only at promotion and read only by pg_rewind and at startup.

Nothing in Postgres today does this job. The single shared archive is the documented way to keep TLI unique (message #22), but messages #23 and #26 show that a check through restore_command followed by asynchronous archiving cannot make TLI selection atomic. pg_rewind has no other way to tell two same-TLI promotions apart. The DCS-supplied TLI or TLI-allocation hook from messages #31 and #32 does not exist yet, and it would not cover promotions that no coordinator manages. Points not checked without the code: how the patch interacts with tools that parse history files, and whether pg_rewind could get the same result from data it already reads.
